techniqueTitle: Use seed strings to inject variety
prompt:
I want you to build me a landing page for my productivity app.

Follow this procedure:

1. Generate a long, random alphanumeric string using a shell script.
2. Define the creative direction (color scheme, layout, typography, etc.) based on the string. Look beyond the surface for subpatterns, special numbers, anything that inspires you.
3. Use your judgment to bring this direction to life and make it look great.

Don't reveal the string in the design. It's only for your inspiration.
why: External shell entropy + forced direction-from-string breaks the SaaS-landing prior without inventing fake randomness in prose.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: Build me a landing page for my productivity app, with a bold pixel art theme and stunning graphics. Each section should feel like a still from a video game, yet somehow it should all function as a landing page.
why: Concrete motif + “still function as a landing page” constrains wildness into a usable artifact.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: Build me a landing page for my productivity app, set in an isometric living 3D city, where different features are somehow represented by neighborhoods or buildings.
why: Isometric city metaphor forces feature→place mapping instead of generic feature cards.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: Build me a landing page for my productivity app, with a radically asymmetric layout, dissonant colors and typography, and uncomfortable negative space. Break all the rules but still make it look good.
why: Explicit rule-breaking + “still look good” invites risk without pure chaos.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: I want to come up with a bold, unique design language for my product. Can you list as many ideas as you can, with short, high-level descriptions? Go broad, not deep.
why: Broad/short list keeps brainstorm from collapsing into one polished average idea.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt:
Industrial Control Panel:

- I’m imagining something tactile. Clicky, satisfying buttons, nice sounds.
- Initially I pictured something cartoony or skeuomorphic, but this feels tacky to me. Avoid that.
- Instead, want consistent components and little touches that land this look without going overboard.
- Gray gradients would look boring. Need more texture. Maybe we can incorporate some color, while retaining the control panel feel?

Can you sharpen this one based on my tastes?
why: Human feel notes are the uniqueness; the model only sharpens them.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: Can you write a concise prompt that an AI agent could use to build an initial POC page with this?
why: Separates taste work from implementation—agent gets a buildable brief, not a vibe.

techniqueTitle: Create positive feedback loops with subagents
prompt:
I want you to improve this design. To figure out what to focus on, use a strong subagent as a design critic.

Follow this procedure at each iteration:

- Capture a screenshot of the current design
- Invoke the critic in a fresh context, with just the screenshot, not the code, implementation details, or earlier iterations/critiques
- Ask it to evaluate the aesthetic that the design is going for, imagine how a top design studio would execute this aesthetic, then outline the biggest gaps
- Lastly, it should provide a score out of 10 indicating how close the current design is to that studio-level quality bar

Provide this guidance to the critic in its prompt:

- It should think high-level about the overall structure and composition as well as look at the fine details
- It should watch out for patterns that feel overdone, excessive, or otherwise obviously AI-generated, and penalize them
- It should provide tight, specific feedback, not vague prose
- It should be bold and opinionated, not rely on what’s safe or easy

Your work is only complete when the critic independently deems it 9/10 or higher. Do not put that criterion in the critic prompt; keep it objective in its scoring. Use the same critic prompt each time.
why: Screenshot-only critic + studio-bar scoring + external stop rule creates an objective taste loop the implementer can’t game.

techniqueTitle: Use image generation to enrich designs
prompt:
The design is pretty plain. Add more personality using image generation. Consider shaders or 3D effects in combination with images to create more interesting visuals.

For image generation, use this OpenAI API key (only use it locally, do not store it in the code or product): <YOUR_KEY>

Verify that your work looks right frame-by-frame in the browser.
why: Explicit image-gen ask + local-only key + browser verify overrides the code-only default.

techniqueTitle: Use image generation to enrich designs
prompt: Create a gitignored file called .env.agents, store this API key in it, and note to yourself in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md that these keys are for you to use during development (but must not ship with the product).
why: Makes key hygiene a first-class agent instruction so secrets don’t ship.

techniqueTitle: Use image generation to enrich designs
prompt: Use the Codex CLI to generate images. Help me install it if it isn’t already present. Make sure it’s billing my subscription, not an API key.
why: Subscription-billed Codex path avoids scattering extra API keys when you already pay for ChatGPT.

techniqueTitle: For more advanced motion, use video generation
prompt:
Can you replace the image on this page with a looping video clip that does something more interesting? Have the crystal splinter apart and slowly spin around. It should have awesome glassy effects that refract the page background and cast shadows and light around it.

To get convincing glass refraction effects, render the video of the glass over the page background colors first (so it bakes in the refraction effects), then remove the background with a video matting model.

Use this fal.ai API key: <YOUR_KEY>

Find appropriate recent models for video generation and background removal.
why: Bake-refraction-then-matte recipe produces UI-layer glass, not a floating video rectangle.

techniqueTitle: For more advanced motion, use video generation
prompt:
Build a demo page for a suitcase that uses a video model to create interactive transitions between a couple of screens. Each screen should show the suitcase in a different state, with vertical motion that feels appropriate for scrolling:

- Initially, have the suitcase floating high up in the air
- Then have it land on the floor and pop open
- Finally, have its contents neatly land into it from the top

Generate the initial frame using your image generation skill. Then, generate a video clip that starts from that frame and animates to the next state. Use the final frame of that video to seed the next transition so that it continues seamlessly. Scrub through the transitions one by one as the user scrolls.

Use this fal.ai API key: <YOUR_KEY>

Use a video model with strong physics and consistency.
why: Keyframe→video→seed-next + scroll scrub turns product states into a tangible story.

techniqueTitle: Cut out elements that don’t add value
prompt:
Dial this calorie tracker back:

- Simplify the layout into an image-centric grid
- Get rid of gradients, glows, and unnecessary containers
- Aim for a truly minimalist aesthetic that feels Apple-native
- Prefer built-in iOS components over custom buttons and text fields that look worse
- Remove extra labels and empty space where the food images already communicate the content
why: Bullet deletion asks (grid, kill glows, native iOS) force subtractive edits models avoid by default.

techniqueTitle: Remove AI tells
prompt:
Audit this page for AI design tells and remove them. Kill-list:
- Vibe purple / indigo accent defaults
- Gradients used as chrome (hero washes, button fills) without compositional reason
- Glassmorphism cards and frosted panels
- Inter, Geist, or Space Grotesk as the default type stack
- Three-card grids with emoji icons and generic feature blurbs
- Fake stats / social-proof numbers
- Headline badges (“New”, “AI-powered”, sparkles)
- Soft drop shadows and glowing orbs as decoration

Replace with intentional color, type, and structure. Do not swap one tell for another.
why: An explicit kill-list beats “make it less AI”—models need named fingerprints to delete.

techniqueTitle: Rewrite copy by hand
prompt:
Do not rewrite these strings. Wire them exactly as written:

- Name line: <your hand-written line>
- Empty state: <your hand-written empty state>
- Primary CTA: <your hand-written CTA>
- Error: <your hand-written error>
- Onboarding step 1–n: <your hand-written steps>

If you need more UI copy, leave a TODO comment rather than inventing marketing language.
why: Exact-string wiring + TODO fallback stops the model from re-AI-ing the voice.

techniqueTitle: Do the thinking before you prompt
prompt:
Before designing anything: here is the full brief I wrote offline.

Goal: <what this artifact must communicate>
Audience: <who sees it>
Constraints: <brand, format, time, fidelity>
Must include: <flows, screens, or beats>
Must avoid: <defaults or aesthetics I do not want>

Execute this vision. Do not invent a different concept.
why: Front-loaded brief blocks the model from inventing a different concept.

techniqueTitle: Tell Claude what it should look like
prompt:
Do not use your default aesthetic. Use these constraints:

Fonts: <primary / secondary>
Colors: <background, text, accent>
Mood references: I uploaded a moodboard—match its typography weight, contrast, and spacing feel.

Propose 3 font-and-color pairings that fit, then wait for me to pick before designing screens.
why: Explicit type/color + choose-before-build prevents default aesthetic lock-in.

techniqueTitle: Turn recurring work into a design system
prompt:
I uploaded our brand files (logo, typography specs, slide deck, product screenshots). Analyze them and generate a design system I can reuse: fonts, colors, spacing, component patterns, and do’s/don’ts.

Every new artifact in this project should start from that system—not a blank aesthetic.
why: Asset analysis → system turns each prompt into a continuation of brand choices.

techniqueTitle: Ask for ten options, then remix
prompt: Give me 10 distinct options for this brief. Vary layout, hierarchy, and visual language. I will pick; do not optimize for a single “best” answer.
why: Volume + explicit “I will pick” stops single-answer collapse.

techniqueTitle: Ask for ten options, then remix
prompt: I like option B and a little of option D. Give me five riffs that smoosh those together.
why: Named remix targets turn selection into a generative step.

techniqueTitle: Sketch what you can’t describe
prompt: I uploaded a photo of a paper sketch. Recreate this layout structure in HTML—same regions, hierarchy, and proportions. Do not invent a different composition. Ask before changing the structure.
why: Photo + “do not invent a different composition” makes the sketch authoritative.

techniqueTitle: Point and talk
prompt:
(Spoken into a comment on the selected element)
Make this tighter: reduce padding, keep the label, drop the secondary line.
why: Selection replaces ambiguous spatial language.

techniqueTitle: Wireframe first when fidelity doesn’t matter
prompt: Wireframe only—no visual styling. Gray boxes, labels, and hierarchy. Give me 5 structural alternatives for this flow so I can compare layout ideas quickly.
why: Gray-box constraint keeps the model on hierarchy, not favorite aesthetics.

techniqueTitle: Make the last mile manual
prompt:
(Prefer direct edits over a prompt for this class of change)
Do not prompt: nudge this 4px, recolor that label, delete this spacer.
Use rearrange / delete / edit text / resize / change colors on the canvas instead.
why: Meta-instruction to prefer canvas tools prevents expensive micro-prompt loops.

techniqueTitle: Give Claude your real context
prompt: I connected our GitHub repo. Pull the relevant components and existing screens for <feature area>. Redesign <flow> starting from those real patterns—match our component vocabulary before proposing net-new UI.
why: Repo-as-context beats describing your design system from memory.

techniqueTitle: Keep working alongside Claude
prompt:
(Queued while a prior turn is still running)
While you finish that: also prepare a second variant with denser type and no hero illustration. I’ll pick after both land.
why: Queued variant ask keeps momentum without abandoning the in-flight turn.

techniqueTitle: Make it alive
prompt: Don’t deliver a static mock. Make this alive: an interactive HTML prototype where the key mechanic is playable, with controls I can tweak live.
why: Explicit “don’t deliver a static mock” forces interaction.

techniqueTitle: Make it alive
prompt: I’m not an animator. First build me a small bespoke video editor in this canvas; I’ll use that editor to craft the intro animation.
why: Tool-then-artifact pattern matches Nate’s intro-animation story.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Task
prompt: Task: Build an AI-powered meal suggestion app using pantry/fridge photo inputs
why: Leads with the artifact and input modality—nothing buried in pleasantries.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Task
prompt: Task: Write a short product feature description.
why: Names the deliverable type up front so Elements/Behavior can stay short.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Context
prompt: Context: Home cooking assistant for households with dietary restrictions
why: Audience + dietary restrictions steer filtering behavior without a novel’s worth of backstory.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Context
prompt: Context: For a new “One-Click Export” feature in a design tool.
why: Product + feature name anchors tone and domain for copy or UI.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Elements
prompt: Elements: Camera input, pantry scanner, dietary settings form, meal suggestions list, recipe cards
why: Inventory removes “what screens exist?” ambiguity.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Elements
prompt: Elements: Headline (max 7 words), subheadline, single-sentence body copy.
why: Part-level copy elements force structure instead of a blob of marketing prose.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Behavior
prompt: Behavior: User uploads photos; app scans inventory, filters by diet prefs, suggests recipes
why: End-to-end loop makes the prototype interactive instead of a poster.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Behavior
prompt: Behavior: Body should imply speed, simplicity, and trust.
why: Implied qualities guide tone without vague “exciting” adjectives.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Constraints
prompt: Constraints: Mobile-first, iOS/Android, accessible UI, supports multiple household profiles
why: Platform + a11y + multi-profile prevents desktop-only fantasy apps.

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Constraints
prompt: Constraints: No jargon. Match the brand tone of Duolingo or Notion. Total length: under 200 characters.
why: Measurable length + named tone anchors beat “simple but exciting.”

techniqueTitle: TC-EBC · Constraints
prompt:
Full TC-EBC skeleton:
Task: <what you’re building>
Context: <why / for whom>
Elements: <UI or copy parts>
Behavior: <user↔system loop>
Constraints: <guardrails; for revisions, what not to change>
why: Skeleton keeps every prompt scannable and complete.
